annotations.description: Only 2 of 3 brokers are reachable; the cluster tolerates one loss.

diagnosis.summary: Chaos Mesh experiment ~133 min ago killed all 3 Kafka broker pods; all restarted, but broker `lakehouse-dual-role-0` JMX endpoint is unresponsive — Prometheus cannot scrape it, keeping the KafkaBrokerDown alert firing. 60 partitions remain under-replicated; no offline or under-min-ISR partitions, so writes continue.
diagnosis.root_cause: A Chaos Mesh pod-kill experiment deployed 133 minutes ago (revision 9187ff9e9e6f) terminated all three Kafka broker pods simultaneously (exit_code 255 / reason Unknown — the Chaos Mesh fingerprint). Brokers 1 and 2 recovered fully. Broker 0 (`lakehouse-dual-role-0`) pod is Running 1/1 (Kafka readiness probe passes) but its JMX/metrics port is unresponsive to Prometheus (`brokers_scraped_up: false`), causing the alert to remain firing. The reported `active_controllers: 0` is a side-effect of broker 0 being the KRaft controller leader but its metrics being unscrapable. The 60 under-replicated partitions are those where broker 0 is a follower and has not yet caught up or is not replicating.
diagnosis.impact: No data loss and no write outage: 0 offline partitions, 0 under-min-ISR partitions. Flink `events-to-iceberg` is RUNNING/STABLE with modest consumer lag (200). The cluster is at minimum redundancy — one more broker loss would stop writes. Broker 0 metrics and KRaft controller-leader visibility are blind.

evidence.finding: All 3 broker pods Running 1/1; brokers_scraped_up shows lakehouse-dual-role-0=false, brokers 1 and 2=true; under_replicated_partitions=60; under_min_isr_partitions=0; offline_partitions=0; active_controllers=0; consumer_lag=200. All brokers show last_termination reason=Unknown exit_code=255 ~129 min ago.
chaos-mesh-local deployed revision 9187ff9e9e6f 133.1 minutes ago — timing matches all broker pod terminations at ~129 min ago and Flink restart at ~127.9 min ago.
Job RUNNING/STABLE, started 127.9 min ago (right after broker recovery), 28.23 completed checkpoints/5m, 0 failed checkpoints, consumer lag 200 — no pipeline failure.
All 3 worker nodes Ready, one per zone, no pressure conditions or cordons — node failure ruled out.
All Argo CD applications Synced and Healthy including chaos-mesh-local, strimzi-local, platform-local.
0 warning events in kafka namespace — no Kubernetes-level errors recorded after recovery.
Runbook docs/runbooks/kafka.md#kafkabrokerdown: Strimzi restarts a crashed broker; check pod/node if Pending; do not delete the PVC.

proposed_action.rationale: Broker 0 is Running 1/1 (Kafka port healthy per readiness probe) but its JMX exporter is unresponsive — consistent with the exporter process crashing silently during the Chaos Mesh pod-kill recovery. Restarting the pod via Strimzi StatefulSet is safe: RF=3 with min.insync.replicas=2 and 2 fully healthy brokers means no write outage during the brief restart. This should clear the JMX scraping failure, resolve the alert, and allow broker 0 to rejoin as a clean replica to close the 60 under-replicated partitions.

follow_ups: Confirm whether the Chaos Mesh experiment (revision 9187ff9e9e6f, deployed ~133 min ago) was intentional; if so, ensure it is deactivated or scoped to avoid simultaneous multi-broker kills which leave the cluster at zero margin.
After broker 0 restarts, verify under_replicated_partitions drops to 0 and active_controllers returns to 1.
Investigate why a simultaneous 3-broker kill left broker 0's JMX exporter non-functional post-restart — consider adding a liveness probe on the JMX port in addition to the Kafka port.
Consumer lag of 200 is small but monitor that Flink clears it after broker 0 fully rejoins the ISR.
A log line in broker 0 logs instructing a configuration change was attempted to be read but was inaccessible — ensure log observability (Loki) for kafka namespace is restored after restart.

reasoning_summaries: Let me investigate the KafkaBrokerDown alert. I'll start by checking multiple things in parallel.

Interesting. All 3 broker pods are Running and Ready (1/1), but `brokers_scraped_up` shows `lakehouse-dual-role-0` as false. This means the metrics scraping for broker 0 is failing, not the broker itself being down. Also:
- 60 under-replicated partitions
- 0 offline partitions
- 0 under-min-ISR partitions
- 0 active controllers (this is concerning!)
- Consumer lag: 200

All brokers had terminations ~129 minutes ago with exit_code 255 (Unknown reason), and broker 1 has only been running for 225 minutes (suggesting it was recently replaced/restarted).
With the alert firing at 07:54:48 UTC, I should check broker 0's logs since its scraping is failing, plus look at Kafka events and Flink job status given the lag. The zero active controllers is especially worrying since in this dual-role setup the brokers also serve as KRaft controllers, so this could directly explain a broker-down condition.

Let me analyze the state:

1. All 3 broker pods are Running and 1/1 Ready
2. `lakehouse-dual-role-0` has metrics scraping failing (brokers_scraped_up = false)
3. 60 under-replicated partitions - this is concerning
4. 0 active controllers - very concerning in KRaft mode
5. All brokers had terminations ~129 minutes ago with exit_code 255
6. Flink job started 127.9 minutes ago (right after the broker restarts)
7. Consumer lag: 200

The alert fired at 07:54:48. All brokers terminated ~129 minutes ago. The Flink job also restarted ~127.9 minutes ago. 

This points to a cluster-wide disruption roughly 129 minutes back where every broker went down together. The zero active controllers is especially worrying in KRaft mode since that count should normally be 1, implying there may be no leader and the cluster could be unable to accept writes. The alert's framing of "2 of 3 brokers reachable" seems tied to broker-0 failing its JMX/Prometheus scrape specifically.

Looking closer, broker 0 shows as not scraped while the other two report fine, even though its pod is Running 1/1 -- meaning the pod itself seems healthy but something's blocking metric collection, possibly a crashed JMX exporter, a network policy problem, or the broker process being unhealthy despite passing readiness checks. Combined with the zero active controllers, I want to pull broker 0's previous logs. The pattern of 60 under-replicated partitions but zero offline and zero under-min-ISR partitions suggests data is still being written fine, just that broker 0 hasn't caught up as a replica yet -- so next I'll dig into its logs and the Prometheus metrics for more clarity.

The logs and metrics for broker 0 are completely unavailable. This is consistent with the broker being unreachable from the metrics/logging infrastructure. Let me try to get more data points from Prometheus and Kafka metrics.

Loki and Prometheus are both unable to return data for kafka-related queries. This is quite unusual. Let me try to get Prometheus for other metrics.

Let me try broader Prometheus queries and check if there's a broader observability issue.

This is very revealing! I can see `chaos-mesh-local` has been deployed multiple times. The most recent relevant event is `chaos-mesh-local` deployed 133.1 minutes ago with revision `9187ff9e9e6f`. This timing correlates with:
- All brokers terminating ~129 minutes ago
- Flink job restarting ~127.9 minutes ago
- The alert firing at 07:54:48

Chaos Mesh is a chaos engineering platform. The deployment 133 minutes ago likely injected a fault that:
1. Killed all 3 Kafka broker pods (exit_code 255, reason Unknown - characteristic of chaos kills)
2. Also killed the Flink job manager with the same exit code and timing.

Now all brokers have restarted, but broker 0 still isn't being scraped by Prometheus since it can't reach its JMX endpoint, which explains why the alert persists. I'm also noting 60 under-replicated partitions with 0 under-min-ISR and 0 offline, plus zero active controllers in this KRaft cluster with dual-role nodes -- that active_controllers reading of 0.0 is a serious concern worth digging into.

In KRaft mode, exactly one broker should report as active controller, so seeing zero across the board likely means broker 0 (the unscraped node) is actually the active controller and we just can't see its metrics, rather than the cluster having truly lost its controller entirely. That second scenario would be catastrophic, but since the Flink job is still running with checkpoints succeeding and consumer lag sitting at only 200, Kafka is clearly still processing metadata changes and handling produce/consume traffic fine -- which supports the theory that broker 0 is the active controller and this is just a monitoring gap.

Piecing it together: a Chaos Mesh experiment roughly 133 minutes ago killed all three broker pods simultaneously; they all restarted successfully, but broker 0's JMX/metrics endpoint remains unreachable from Prometheus, which is why brokers_scraped_up shows false for that node and the alert keeps firing even though the pod itself is Running 1/1. They all restarted, but broker 0's JMX metrics port never came back up, so Prometheus can't scrape it and the alert keeps firing; the under-replicated partitions are probably ones where broker 0 is still catching up as a follower, and the missing controller metric is the same scraping gap if broker 0 is the KRaft leader. My plan is to restart broker 0 since it's safe with two healthy brokers and RF=3/min ISR=2 — Strimzi should recreate it cleanly.
